- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast spikes upward, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment drops sharply (≤0.4) after a spike, model should not overshoot downward; cap decline to avoid excessive sell-off.  
- Forecast mean should align with recent 7–14 day average, especially when sentiment is neutral or low.  
- Overshoots in early forecast days (e.g., day 1–3) are common; apply a 3–5% downward adjustment if sentiment is weak.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 75), model should reduce forecast volatility and shift toward historical range.  
- When sentiment is high but price drops sharply, model should not assume continuation; add a 2–3 day lagged correction buffer.  
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid extreme highs/lows if sentiment is mixed (0.4–0.7); use sentiment-weighted smoothing to dampen outliers.
